name: dusty packed wasteland earth ground, a seamless 4x4-tile field with soft clumped earth patches, soft darker blotches and faint wheel ruts running across tile borders, mixed with tiles of dry grass tufts
label: wasteland_ruins/dirt-d

surfaces.part: packed earth ground field with grass tufts

answer.evidence: This is a seamless terrain field, 96 px wide for all rows 0-79. It has no silhouette, front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or vertical face. The column scans show only mottled brown earth noise (L 60-118) with small yellow-green grass tufts at rows 8-10, 24-28, 42-46, 54-59 and 74-79. There is no standing body, so the field is a flat top-down ground texture with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown packed-earth field with mottled blotches and small yellow dry-grass tufts. Measured facts: 4 visible tones per tile against 3 for the reference grass and 7 for the paving, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edges. It has no outlines, so nothing reads as a sticker. Its earth ramp has about 4 steps (light, mid, dark, deep) against 5-6 in the references. The mottling is soft and fairly uniform, with little per-clump highlighting or grain. The tufts are sparse and small. The wheel ruts and clumped patches asked for are barely visible. It has no flat fills, but it is a little thinner and less crafted than the references, and only the grass reference is matched on tone count. Because the ground is generally even and the ruts are not readable, this is not clearly equal to the Beodeul bar. When in doubt, fail.
